grammar.title: State a considered conclusion
grammar.formation: Plain proposition + と言える/と言えます. A complete noun/な-adjective proposition normally uses だ: 妥当だと言える. と言えるだろう softens the conclusion.
grammar.explanation: と言える presents a conclusion or evaluation the writer considers justified: “it is fair to say.” It uses the potential of 言う, not the passive hearsay と言われている. It does not turn the writer’s evaluation into a guarantee. Quote the whole proposition before と; use だ in a noun or な-adjective predicate when teaching a complete clause. This intermediate bridge is retrieved in N2 argument writing; publisher tags vary.
grammar.example: この経費なら、参加費は妥当だと言える。
grammar.translation: Given these expenses, the participation fee can be considered reasonable.

examples.ja: この{経費|けいひ}なら、{参加|さんか}{費|ひ}は{妥当|だとう}だと{言|い}える。
examples.en: Given these expenses, the participation fee can be considered reasonable.

examples.ja: {二十人|にじゅうにん}が{予約|よやく}したので、{関心|かんしん}を{集|あつ}めたと{言|い}える。
examples.en: With twenty bookings, it’s fair to say the event attracted interest.

examples.ja: {二|ふた}つの{案|あん}には{共通|きょうつう}{点|てん}があると{言|い}えるだろう。
examples.en: We could say that the two proposals have points in common.

grammar.mistake: Do not confuse 言える with the hearsay passive 言われている, or write 妥当なと言える for a complete quoted predicate.

grammar.title: An action forced by the circumstances
grammar.formation: Verb negative stem (remove ない) + ざるを得ない. する → せざるを得ない; 来る → こざるを得ない. Polite 得ません and past 得なかった are possible.
grammar.explanation: ざるを得ない means there is no practical choice but to act, often reluctantly. It is comparatively formal and useful in an explanation or written opinion. A lack of affordable space may force cancellation; it is not the same as being unable to suppress laughter. Retrieve ないわけにはいかない, which often foregrounds responsibility or an obligation. These meanings can overlap; questions request a form or give an explicit cause rather than rejecting a sensible synonym.
grammar.example: 会場が使えないため、予定を変えざるを得ない。
grammar.translation: The venue’s unavailable, so we have no choice but to change the plan.

examples.ja: {会場|かいじょう}が{使|つか}えないため、{予定|よてい}を{変|か}えざるを{得|え}ない。
examples.en: The venue’s unavailable, so we have no choice but to change the plan.

examples.ja: {経費|けいひ}が{足|た}りず、{規模|きぼ}を{縮小|しゅくしょう}せざるを{得|え}なかった。
examples.en: We lacked funds and had to reduce the scale.

examples.ja: {代案|だいあん}がなければ、{今回|こんかい}は{中止|ちゅうし}せざるを{得|え}ません。
examples.en: If there’s no alternative, we’ll have to cancel this time.

grammar.mistake: する uses せざる, not しざる. Do not append ざる to a dictionary form such as 変更するざる. The double negative requires doing the action.

grammar.title: Limit a claim to just that amount or role
grammar.formation: Noun or plain verb clause + にすぎない/にすぎません; written に過ぎない. Noun + である is also possible. For a な-adjective use なだけ or である before the pattern.
grammar.explanation: にすぎない limits the importance, quantity or extent of what precedes it: “merely” or “no more than.” It is not the same as すぎる meaning excessively. A count can be “only five”; an opinion can be “just one aspect.” To avoid variable adjective attachments in early practice, use nouns, ordinary verb clauses and the explicit なだけ/である variants. It is not automatically a denial of the whole activity’s value.
grammar.example: 集めた参加費で払えるのは、経費の一部にすぎない。
grammar.translation: The participation fees cover only part of the expenses.

examples.ja: {集|あつ}めた{参加|さんか}{費|ひ}で{払|はら}えるのは、{経費|けいひ}の{一部|いちぶ}にすぎない。
examples.en: The participation fees cover only part of the expenses.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{一人|ひとり}の{参加|さんか}{者|しゃ}にすぎません。
まだ{案|あん}を{出|だ}したにすぎず、{決定|けってい}はしていない。
examples.en: We’ve only put forward a proposal; nothing’s been decided.

grammar.mistake: Do not treat にすぎない as an excessive action or attach a present noun with だにすぎない. Read exactly what it limits.

grammar.title: Hear a strong conviction, not a report
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + に違いない. Noun/な-adjective stem + に違いない without present だ. Past だった clauses are possible; polite に違いありません.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the N3 conviction pattern. A speaker is strongly convinced by the situation, but に違いない itself is not a report of checking. For example, seeing umbrellas may lead someone to think it must be raining. In an argument it may express confidence about an effect; read that confidence separately from a stated outcome.
grammar.example: 傘がぬれている。外は雨に違いない。
grammar.translation: The umbrella’s wet. It must be raining outside.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}がぬれている。{外|そと}は{雨|あめ}に{違|ちが}いない。
examples.en: The umbrella’s wet. It must be raining outside.

examples.ja: {会場|かいじょう}を{見|み}つけられたら、みんな{喜|よろこ}ぶに{違|ちが}いない。
examples.en: If we find a venue, I’m sure everyone will be pleased.

examples.ja: あの{大|おお}きな{荷物|にもつ}は{会|かい}の{道具|どうぐ}だったに{違|ちが}いない。
examples.en: That large load must have been equipment for the event.

grammar.mistake: Use 静かに違いない or 雨に違いない, not 静かなに違いない or 雨だに違いない. Do not score conviction as confirmed attendance or feelings.

grammar.title: Add a further fact for emphasis
grammar.formation: Plain verb/い-adjective + ばかりか; な-adjective + な/であるばかりか; noun + ばかりか/であるばかりか.
grammar.explanation: ばかりか adds another, often stronger, fact: “not only … but also ….” It is more written or emphatic than だけでなく, retrieved from N3. Both favourable and unfavourable facts are possible. Teach a factual or descriptive second clause; requests and invitations do not fit the taught use. This connector does not express a contrast or say the first point is unimportant.
grammar.example: 経費が増えたばかりか、準備の時間も足りなくなった。
grammar.translation: Not only did expenses rise, we also ran short of preparation time.

examples.ja: {経費|けいひ}が{増|ふ}えたばかりか、{準備|じゅんび}の{時間|じかん}も{足|た}りなくなった。
examples.en: Not only did expenses rise, we also ran short of preparation time.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{静|しず}かなばかりか、{駅|えき}からも{近|ちか}い。
examples.en: The room’s not only quiet, it’s also close to the station.

examples.ja: その{案|あん}は{妥当|だとう}であるばかりか、{実行|じっこう}しやすい。
examples.en: The proposal’s not only reasonable but also easy to put into practice.

grammar.mistake: The な-adjective needs な or である here. Use a statement in the second clause, not a direct request. Do not force ばかりか versus だけでなく as exclusive answers when either fits.

dialogues.title: Can we keep the reading group affordable?
dialogues.scene: Misaki and Bao plan a small Saturday reading group at the library. The room is free, but printed material costs three thousand yen. They discuss a two-hundred-yen fee and a way to welcome first-time participants.

lines.romaji: Dokusho kai no heya, muryō de karirareru tte.
lines.meaning: They say we can use the reading-group room for free.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: よかった。{印刷|いんさつ}の{経費|けいひ}は{三千円|さんぜんえん}くらいだよね。
lines.romaji: Yokatta. Insatsu no keihi wa sanzen en kurai da yo ne.
lines.meaning: Great. Printing will cost about three thousand yen, right?

lines.romaji: Un. Sanka hi, nihyaku en ni suru?
lines.meaning: Yes. Shall we charge two hundred yen to join?

lines.meaning: Twenty people would bring in four thousand yen, but will it be full?

lines.romaji: Mada wakannai ne. Shūshi o mite kara, tsugi no ryōkin o kimeyō.
lines.meaning: We don’t know yet. Let’s look at what comes in and goes out before setting the next fee.

lines.romaji: Annai ni wa datō na ryōkin da to ieru tte kaita kedo, katai?
lines.meaning: I wrote “the fee can be considered reasonable” in the notice. Too stiff?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。「{印刷|いんさつ}{代|だい}として{二百円|にひゃくえん}」でいいんじゃない？
lines.romaji: Un. Insatsu dai to shite nihyaku en de ii n ja nai?
lines.meaning: Yes. How about just “two hundred yen towards printing”?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうだね。{初|はじ}めての{人|ひと}が{入|はい}りやすい{代案|だいあん}もないかな。
lines.romaji: Sō da ne. Hajimete no hito ga hairiyasui daian mo nai kana.
lines.meaning: Good point. Is there another option that makes it easier for newcomers?

lines.speaker: Misaki

lines.romaji: Shokai dake muryō ni suru to ka. Tarinai bun wa, sākuru no yosan kara.
lines.meaning: Their first visit could be free. The club budget could cover the shortfall.

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Yosan, tsukatte ii ka kikanakya ne.
lines.meaning: We’ll need to ask if we can use it.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {反論|はんろん}があったら、その{理由|りゆう}も{聞|き}こう。{会|かい}を{続|つづ}けたいのは{同|おな}じだし。
lines.romaji: Hanron ga attara, sono riyū mo kikō. Kai o tsuzuketai no wa onaji da shi.
lines.meaning: If anyone objects, let’s hear why. We all want the group to keep going.

lines.romaji: Un. Mazu wa gensoku nihyaku en, shokai muryō wa sōdan chū tte koto de.
lines.meaning: Right. Two hundred yen as the general fee, with free first visits still under discussion.

dialogues.title: Cancel once, or move the group indoors?
dialogues.scene: For a later outdoor reading event, the forecast is heavy rain. Ren and Bao have no indoor room confirmed. They can contact the library by noon; if no room is available, they will cancel this one event and try again next month.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {土曜|どよう}、{大雨|おおあめ}だって。{公園|こうえん}で{読|よ}むのは{無理|むり}そう。
lines.romaji: Doyō, ōame da tte. Kōen de yomu no wa muri sō.
lines.meaning: They’re forecasting heavy rain on Saturday. Reading in the park doesn’t look possible.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {屋内|おくない}の{代案|だいあん}、まだないよね。
lines.romaji: Okunai no daian, mada nai yo ne.
lines.meaning: We haven’t got an indoor alternative yet, have we?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: うん。{図書館|としょかん}の{部屋|へや}が{空|あ}いてるか、お{昼|ひる}までに{聞|き}いてみる。
lines.romaji: Un. Toshokan no heya ga aiteru ka, ohiru made ni kiite miru.
lines.meaning: No. I’ll ask by noon whether the library has a room free.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {取|と}れなかったら、{今回|こんかい}は{中止|ちゅうし}せざるを{得|え}ないね。
lines.romaji: Torenakattara, konkai wa chūshi sezaru o enai ne.
lines.meaning: If we can’t get one, we’ll have to cancel this time.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: そうだね。{暫定|ざんてい}{的|てき}な{案内|あんない}だけでも{先|さき}に{出|だ}そう。
lines.romaji: Sō da ne. Zantei teki na annai dake demo saki ni dasō.
lines.meaning: Yes. Let’s at least put out a provisional update first.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「{会|かい}の{存続|そんぞく}が{難|むずか}しい」って{書|か}くと、もう{終|お}わりみたいじゃない？
lines.romaji: Kai no sonzoku ga muzukashii tte kaku to, mō owari mitai ja nai?
lines.meaning: Writing “the group’s future is in doubt” makes it sound like we’re stopping for good, doesn’t it?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: あ、それは{違|ちが}う。{今回|こんかい}だけだよ。{来月|らいげつ}はやりたい。
lines.romaji: A, sore wa chigau. Konkai dake da yo. Raigetsu wa yaritai.
lines.meaning: Oh, that’s not what we mean. Just this time. I’d like to hold it next month.

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Ja, konkai no okugai kaisai ni tsuite tte daimei ni shiyō.
lines.meaning: Then let’s call it “About This Outdoor Event.”

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: いいね。{予定|よてい}の{一部|いちぶ}が{変|か}わるだけって{分|わ}かる。
lines.romaji: Ii ne. Yotei no ichibu ga kawaru dake tte wakaru.
lines.meaning: Good. That makes clear we’re only changing part of the programme.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {部屋|へや}が{取|と}れたら、みんな{喜|よろこ}ぶに{違|ちが}いない。あの{話|はなし}の{続|つづ}き、{聞|き}きたいな。
lines.romaji: Heya ga toretara, minna yorokobu ni chigai nai. Ano hanashi no tsuzuki, kikitai na.
lines.meaning: If we get a room, I’m sure everyone will be pleased. I want to hear the rest of that story.

lines.romaji: Ore mo. Denwa shitara, sugu renraku suru ne.
lines.meaning: Me too. I’ll let you know as soon as I’ve called.

lines.romaji: Arigatō. Sore made yoyaku shita hito ni mo, henkō no kanōsei o shirasetoku.
lines.meaning: Thanks. In the meantime, I’ll warn the people who booked that the plan may change.

readings.title: A fee that keeps the door open
paragraphs: {読書|どくしょ}{会|かい}の{参加|さんか}{費|ひ}を{無料|むりょう}にするべきだという{意見|いけん}がある。{初|はじ}めての{人|ひと}が{入|はい}りやすくなるという{点|てん}は、{確|たし}かに{大切|たいせつ}だ。{私|わたし}も{参加|さんか}をためらう{人|ひと}を{減|へ}らしたい。しかし、{全員|ぜんいん}を{毎回|まいかい}{無料|むりょう}にする{案|あん}には{反論|はんろん}がある。

{部屋|へや}は{無料|むりょう}でも、{資料|しりょう}の{印刷|いんさつ}には{三千円|さんぜんえん}かかる。{二百円|にひゃくえん}ずつ{集|あつ}めれば、{二十人|にじゅうにん}で{四千円|よんせんえん}になる。ただし、これは{満席|まんせき}という{仮定|かてい}の{計算|けいさん}である。{人数|にんずう}が{減|へ}れば、{収支|しゅうし}も{変|か}わる。{経費|けいひ}を{主催|しゅさい}{者|しゃ}だけが{払|はら}う{形|かたち}では、{長|なが}く{続|つづ}けにくい。{一定|いってい}の{参加|さんか}{費|ひ}は{妥当|だとう}だと{言|い}える。

{一方|いっぽう}、{費用|ひよう}の{説明|せつめい}だけでは、{初|はじ}めて{来|く}る{人|ひと}の{心配|しんぱい}はなくならないだろう。そこで、{原則|げんそく}は{二百円|にひゃくえん}とし、{初回|しょかい}だけ{無料|むりょう}にする{代案|だいあん}を{考|かんが}えた。{不足|ふそく}する{分|ぶん}はサークルの{予算|よさん}で{補|おぎな}えないか、{相談|そうだん}したい。この{案|あん}はまだ{決|き}まっていない。{認|みと}められなければ、{別|べつ}の{方法|ほうほう}を{考|かんが}えざるを{得|え}ない。

{私|わたし}が{主張|しゅちょう}したいのは、{料金|りょうきん}の{安|やす}さだけを{目的|もくてき}にしないということだ。{収支|しゅうし}を{明|あき}らかにし、{気軽|きがる}に{試|ため}せる{機会|きかい}も{作|つく}る。{二|ふた}つの{考|かんが}えを{組|く}み{合|あ}わせた{案|あん}のほうが、{会|かい}を{続|つづ}ける{方法|ほうほう}として{説得力|せっとくりょく}があると{思|おも}う。

readings.title: One cancellation is not the end
paragraphs: {屋外|おくがい}の{読書|どくしょ}{会|かい}を{中止|ちゅうし}するかどうか、{私|わたし}たちは{迷|まよ}っている。{土曜日|どようび}は{大雨|おおあめ}の{予報|よほう}で、{公園|こうえん}の{屋根|やね}も{小|ちい}さい。{私|わたし}は、{別|べつ}の{会場|かいじょう}が{見|み}つからなければ、{今回|こんかい}の{開催|かいさい}は{見送|みおく}るべきだと{考|かんが}える。ぬれた{資料|しりょう}を{読|よ}ませるばかりか、{寒|さむ}い{中|なか}で{長|なが}く{待|ま}たせることにもなるからだ。

{予約|よやく}した{人|ひと}をがっかりさせたくないという{意見|いけん}もある。{準備|じゅんび}を{続|つづ}けてきた{人|ひと}ほど、その{思|おも}いは{強|つよ}いに{違|ちが}いない。しかし、{一度|いちど}の{中止|ちゅうし}は、{活動|かつどう}の{一部|いちぶ}の{変更|へんこう}にすぎない。{会|かい}そのものを{廃止|はいし}する{必要|ひつよう}はない。{無理|むり}をして{開|ひら}くことが、{会|かい}の{存続|そんぞく}につながるとも{限|かぎ}らない。

{代案|だいあん}として、{図書館|としょかん}の{部屋|へや}を{使|つか}えないか{確認|かくにん}している。{正午|しょうご}までに{返事|へんじ}をもらい、{使|つか}える{場合|ばあい}は{場所|ばしょ}の{変更|へんこう}を{連絡|れんらく}する。{使|つか}えない{場合|ばあい}は{今回|こんかい}だけ{中止|ちゅうし}し、{来月|らいげつ}の{予定|よてい}は{改|あらた}めて{相談|そうだん}する。まだ{部屋|へや}は{確保|かくほ}できていないので、{屋内|おくない}{開催|かいさい}を{約束|やくそく}する{告知|こくち}は{出|だ}せない。

{私|わたし}にとって{大切|たいせつ}なのは、{続|つづ}けたい{気持|きも}ちを{一日|いちにち}の{開催|かいさい}と{同|おな}じものにしないことだ。{今回|こんかい}は{休|やす}んでも、{次|つぎ}に{読|よ}みたい{話|はなし}を{考|かんが}えられる。{暫定|ざんてい}{的|てき}な{変更|へんこう}を{伝|つた}えるときこそ、{何|なに}を{変|か}え、{何|なに}を{続|つづ}けるのかを{具体|ぐたい}{的|てき}に{書|か}くべきである。

exercises.prompt: What costs money even though the room is free?
options: Printing the material
Renting the room by the hour
A compulsory membership card
exercises.explain: Bao checks printing costs, about three thousand yen.

options: Using the club budget to cover free first visits
Charging a fee of two thousand yen
Making the event free for everyone forever
exercises.explain: Bao says they need to ask whether the budget can be used. The provisional general fee is two hundred yen.

exercises.prompt: How does Misaki suggest simplifying the notice?
options: State two hundred yen towards printing
Call it a permanently profitable investment
Remove any mention of money
exercises.explain: She prefers the practical printing-cost wording to the stiff written evaluation.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the quoted な-adjective proposition before と言える.
exercises.line: この{経費|けいひ}なら、{料金|りょうきん}は＿＿と{言|い}える。
options: {妥当|だとう}だ
{妥当|だとう}な
{妥当|だとう}に
exercises.explain: The quoted predicate is 妥当だ. な modifies a noun; に is adverbial.

exercises.context: Form practice: use ざるを得ない with 変更する.
exercises.line: {会場|かいじょう}が{使|つか}えないので、{予定|よてい}を＿＿。
options: {変更|へんこう}せざるを{得|え}ない
{変更|へんこう}しざるを{得|え}ない
{変更|へんこう}するざるを{得|え}ない
exercises.explain: する uses the exceptional せざる, not しざる or a dictionary-form attachment.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. Agree that you must ask before spending the club budget.
exercises.line: {初回|しょかい}だけ{無料|むりょう}にして、サークルの{予算|よさん}を{使|つか}うのはどう？
options: いいね。でも、{使|つか}っていいか{先|さき}に{聞|き}こう。
もう{許可|きょか}が{出|で}たんだね。すぐ{使|つか}おう。
じゃ、{全員|ぜんいん}を{永久|えいきゅう}に{無料|むりょう}にしよう。
exercises.explain: The first welcomes the proposal while keeping the permission step still needed.

exercises.meaning: Given these expenses, the participation fee can be considered reasonable.
exercises.explain: The quoted judgment keeps the な-adjective predicate だ before と.

exercises.prompt: Which position best matches the writer’s main claim?
options: Combine a general fee with a chance for newcomers to try, and make the finances clear
Make every visit free regardless of who pays the expenses
Charge as much as possible because profit is the only goal
exercises.explain: The final paragraph joins transparent income/expenses and an easy first opportunity.

exercises.prompt: What condition produces the four-thousand-yen figure?
options: Twenty people each paying two hundred yen
Ten people each paying two hundred yen
Twenty people attending free of charge
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly identifies full attendance as an assumption.

exercises.prompt: If budget support is not approved, what must the writer do?
options: Consider another way
Spend the budget without permission
Abolish the club immediately
exercises.explain: The third paragraph says 別の方法を考えざるを得ない.

exercises.prompt: What will Ren do by noon?
options: Ask whether the library has a room free
Confirm that the library room is already booked
Announce that the group is permanently closed
exercises.explain: The room has not been secured. Ren will ask, then report back.

exercises.prompt: If no room can be found, how much of the programme will change?
options: This outdoor event will be cancelled; they want to meet next month
Every future meeting will stop permanently
Only the final sentence of the story will be removed
exercises.explain: Ren corrects the misleading survival wording: 今回だけ, 来月はやりたい.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao’s みんな喜ぶに違いない express?
options: Confidence about how people would feel if they get a room
A report that everybody has already approved the room
A request to close the library
exercises.explain: The room is still conditional; Bao expects a positive reaction.

exercises.context: Form practice: use にすぎない after a noun phrase.
exercises.line: {今回|こんかい}の{中止|ちゅうし}は、{予定|よてい}の{一部|いちぶ}＿＿。
options: にすぎない
だにすぎない
をすぎない
exercises.explain: The noun phrase 一部 takes にすぎない directly. It limits the scope to part of the programme.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete a present noun proposition with に違いない.
exercises.line: {傘|かさ}がぬれている。{外|そと}は＿＿。
options: {雨|あめ}に{違|ちが}いない
{雨|あめ}だに{違|ちが}いない
{雨|あめ}なに{違|ちが}いない
exercises.explain: A present noun attaches directly, without だ or な. This is a conviction from the wet umbrella.

exercises.context: Form practice: attach ばかりか to the な-adjective 静か.
exercises.line: その{部屋|へや}は＿＿、{駅|えき}からも{近|ちか}い。
options: {静|しず}かなばかりか
{静|しず}かだばかりか
{静|しず}かにばかりか
exercises.explain: The な-adjective needs な before this connector; the next clause adds another favourable fact.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Ren before the call. Agree to warn people of a possible change, without claiming a room is confirmed.
exercises.line: お{昼|ひる}までに、{部屋|へや}が{空|あ}いてるか{聞|き}いてみる。
options: ありがとう。それまで、{変更|へんこう}の{可能|かのう}{性|せい}だけ{伝|つた}えておくね。
よかった。もう{屋内|おくない}の{場所|ばしょ}が{決|き}まったね。
じゃ、{来月|らいげつ}も{絶対|ぜったい}に{中止|ちゅうし}だね。
exercises.explain: The first keeps the room enquiry pending and communicates only the possible change.

options: Find an indoor alternative by noon, or cancel this time while keeping future plans open
Keep the outdoor event at any cost to prove commitment
End all future activity even if a room becomes available
exercises.explain: The third paragraph sets the conditional plan; the final paragraph separates continuing the group from one day’s event.

exercises.prompt: What two problems are joined by ばかりか in the first paragraph?
options: Wet reading material and a long wait in the cold
Higher entry fees and permanent abolition
A free room and a warmer forecast
exercises.explain: The clause adds waiting in the cold to being made to read wet material.

exercises.prompt: Why can’t the organisers promise an indoor event yet?
options: They have not secured a room
The writer wants to end the entire group
The workshop has already finished
exercises.explain: The third paragraph explicitly says the room is not yet secured.

recycling.reason: This opinion unit naturally retrieves only a small fraction of recent notice and administrative targets: 原則, 題名 and the notice reference in its reading. Earlier familiar event, budget and booking words recur, but unrelated recent headwords are not inserted into friends’ talk to satisfy a numerical quota.

grammar: a considered conclusion と言える
unavoidable action ざるを得ない
watch.prompt: Optionally read an opinion in your own media. Underline the main recommendation and the reason given for it. Find one limitation, condition or added fact. Save useful lines with their context; a prediction is not an observed result.
